pr.title: List a loop's open pull requests above the Claude Code prompt
pr.head: 20e8905bec3da8c286ee252be402d33f153ec1e5

summary: Projector's fix and review loops each run a watcher script in the background: watch-prs.sh for a review loop and watch-threads.sh for a fix loop. Each watcher reads a tracked file, a plain text file with one owner/repo#number line for each pull request the loop owns. Until now, to see which pull requests a loop watches and which of them need work, you read that file and looked each pull request up on GitHub.

This pull request adds a Claude Code hooks module: TypeScript that Claude Code loads from a plugin's hooks/ directory and runs on engine events, such as a tool call or a slash command. The module lists open pull requests in the band above the prompt, a strip of the terminal directly above the input that spans its width and is only as tall as its lines. Each pull request takes one line: a link, draft or ready, the title, and any conflict, change request, or open threads. The lines sit under two labels. Watching covers pull requests that fix-loop watchers (watch-threads.sh) track, and Reviewing covers those that review-loop watchers (watch-prs.sh) track.

• When the band shows. It stays hidden until the session first runs a watcher it has not seen, through the Bash or Monitor tool, or until you run /loop-prs, which shows or hides it. Claude Code's own [-] collapses it.
  • How it finds loops. It reads each watcher command's --tracked argument, and it scans ps for watchers that other sessions started. /loop-prs <file> adds a tracked file by hand.
  • When it reloads. It reloads when a watcher's notification reaches the session, when a turn ends, and every 30 seconds. Each reload makes one gh api graphql call, and only while the band is shown.
  • What it leaves alone. The module is Claude Code packaging only. No skill depends on it, and Codex gets nothing new.
The validation gate gains claude plugin test ., which runs the module's *.test.ts files.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, of 742c923, opened two findings about the watcher command the session runs itself. One found that variables assigned in the same command did not expand. The other found that a restarted watcher reopened a closed pane. ac89f58 fixed both.
  • 20e8905 moves the list from a docked pane into the band above the prompt. Its review is clean, with both findings still fixed, and the gate passed, with claude plugin test . at 19 of 19.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Watcher: the shell script a loop runs in the background, watch-prs.sh or watch-threads.sh.
  • Tracked file: the file a watcher reads, one owner/repo#number per line. A !owner/repo#number line keeps that pull request out.
  • Hooks module: a plugin's TypeScript that Claude Code runs on engine events.
  • Band: the AbovePrompt region directly above the prompt input, where one plugin can draw.

groups.title: Packaging the hooks module for Claude Code only
groups.kicker: Where Claude Code finds the module, and the state it keeps
intro: Claude Code finds hooks/hooks.json at the plugin root by itself, and that file names the module's entry point, register.tsx. The Claude manifest adds a types field that points at hooks/types.d.ts, the module's state contract. That file declares the two values the module keeps in plugin state: the loops the session has seen, and the last snapshot it drew.
The Codex manifest does not change, and a new packaging test checks that it names neither types nor hooks.

files.note: Adds types, pointing at the module's state contract.
Names register.tsx as the module Claude Code loads.
The pull request and snapshot shapes, and the projector plugin-state keys: seenLoops, loopSnapshot, loopNow, and isLoopBandShown, which records whether the band is shown.
Checks that the module and its contract exist, and that only the Claude manifest declares them.

groups.title: Reading watcher commands and tracked files
groups.kicker: Pure functions that find a watcher's tracked path and read the file
intro: The module learns a loop from a shell command, either the one the session ran or a line of ps output. tokenize splits the command into words and operators, and it records which parts of each word were quoted. findWatchers looks for a word whose last path segment is watch-prs.sh or watch-threads.sh. It then reads that command's --tracked value and stops at the next operator, such as ; or &&.

expand expands a leading ~ and $NAME outside single quotes. A variable that the command assigns before the watcher, as in D=~/loops; watch-prs.sh --tracked $D/tracked, expands ahead of the environment. expand gives up on a command substitution or an unknown variable, so the caller can tell the person to add the file by hand. parseTracked reads the tracked file with the same entry pattern the watchers use, and like watch-prs.sh it matches entries and ! exclusions without regard to case.

files.note: The tokenizer, path expansion, watcher detection, and tracked-file parser.

checks.text: A command that sets its tracked path through variables earlier in the command now resolves. The first review had found that it did not. A new test runs this machine's own loop command, D=~/.local/state/projector; ID=…; bash …/watch-prs.sh --tracked $D/$ID.tracked, and gets the expanded path, and claude plugin test . passed.
keyOf lowercases, so the GitHub response, the previous snapshot, and the tracked entries all key one pull request the same way.

files.note: Covers watcher detection, expansion, the tracked-file parser, and the GitHub query and response.

groups.title: Asking GitHub for every pull request at once
groups.kicker: One GraphQL query, and a reader that tolerates a missing pull request
intro: buildQuery groups the pull requests by repository and gives each one an alias, so one gh api graphql call fetches all of them. Repository names come from parseTracked, which admits only the characters GitHub allows in a name, so they are safe inside the query's string literals.
parseResponse keeps whatever data came back. A pull request that does not exist leaves its slot null and adds an error, but the call fails only when no data came back at all.

files.note: Builds the query and reads its answer into PullRequest records.

checks.text: reviewThreads(first: 100) reads only the first 100 threads, so the open-thread count is too low on a pull request with more.

groups.title: The hooks and the band above the prompt
groups.kicker: Learning loops from tool calls, reloading, and drawing the band
intro: register.tsx wires the module to Claude Code events:

• session.start registers /loop-prs and starts a five-second tick. While the band is shown, the tick moves the band's "updated … ago" text on and reloads once the last load is 30 seconds old.
  • tool.call for Bash and Monitor lets the tool run first, then passes the command to adopt. adopt records each watcher's tracked file and shows the band only for a loop the session has not seen. A .catch handler replays the tool's result, so a failure in the hook never runs the tool twice.
  • prompt.submit and turn.complete schedule a reload when a watcher's notification arrives and when a turn ends.
  • command.run for /loop-prs hides the band when it is shown and shows it otherwise. With a tracked file as its argument, it records the file and shows the band.
  • ui.render for AbovePrompt draws a divider carrying the reload time, then one line per open pull request. It passes to the engine while the band is hidden or a survey holds it.

load merges the session's own loops with watchers that ps found, reads each tracked file, and makes one GitHub call for every pull request. When that call fails, the band keeps what GitHub returned last time. A reload requested during a load runs once more after it.

files.note: The event hooks, the reload logic, and the band's drawing.

checks.text: A watcher that restarts with the same command, as a Monitor does each time it expires, does not show a band that you hid. remember reports whether it added the tracked file, and this line shows the band only then. The test "keeps a band you hid hidden when a known watcher starts again" covers it, and claude plugin test . passed.
A request that arrives during a load sets isQueued, and the load runs once more when it ends. A non-forced reload loads only while isLoopBandShown is true.
The divider's dashes and the "updated … ago" text add up to exactly bodyColumns, so the divider ends where the engine draws [-]. Read at this head. The tests check the width, not the screen.

files.note: Drives watcher commands and /loop-prs through the engine, answers ps, file reads, and gh from memory, and checks the band's lines, the empty state, and when the band shows or stays hidden.
